$comment: Conditional logic engine (spec §1.2). Rules are data, not code, so a non-engineer can read and edit them and so every generation can record which fired.

rules.code: IF [founders >= 2] THEN [include transfer restrictions + buy-sell]
rules.rationale: Multiple owners create exit, death, and divorce scenarios that need a pre-agreed mechanism.

rules.code: IF [founders == 1] THEN [skip buy-sell, add sole-owner provisions]
rules.rationale: A single-owner entity has no counterparty to buy out; different formalities apply.

rules.code: IF [founders == 2] THEN [add deadlock resolution]
rules.rationale: An even two-way split has no tiebreak by default, so any disagreement can freeze the company.

rules.code: IF [entity == LLC] THEN [use LLC statutory forms]
rules.rationale: LLC and corporate governance use different instruments and different vocabulary.

rules.code: IF [entity == C-Corp] THEN [use corporate forms]
rules.rationale: Corporations require authorized stock, a board, and bylaws rather than an operating agreement.

rules.code: IF [formation state != operating state] THEN [add foreign qualification]
rules.rationale: Operating in a state you did not form in generally requires registering there before transacting business.

rules.code: IF [industry is IP-critical] THEN [include IP assignment + data provisions]
rules.rationale: Software, commerce, and health businesses carry their value in intellectual property and data.

rules.code: IF [industry is regulated] THEN [add licensure and compliance provisions]
rules.rationale: Regulated practice areas restrict who may own the entity and how services may be delivered.

rules.code: IF [funding is institutional] THEN [4-year vesting, 1-year cliff, drag-along]
rules.rationale: Standard institutional terms. Deviating from them costs time in diligence without buying anything.

rules.code: IF [entity == C-Corp] AND [vesting applies] THEN [generate 83(b) election]
rules.rationale: The Section 83(b) election must be filed within 30 days of grant. The deadline is not extendable.

rules.code: IF [hiring within 12 months] THEN [include employment policy set]
rules.rationale: Wage-and-hour exposure begins at the first hire, not at scale.

rules.code: IF [operating state == CA] THEN [flag non-compete void + CA policies]
rules.rationale: California voids most employee non-competes (Bus. & Prof. Code §16600; AB 1076 effective January 2024).

rules.code: IF [hiring] AND [operating state == CA] THEN [meal, rest, PTO accrual policies]
rules.rationale: California wage orders require these specific policies; the spec names this exact case in §2.1.

rules.code: IF [formation state == NY] AND [entity == LLC] THEN [publication requirement]
rules.rationale: NY LLC Law §206 requires newspaper publication within 120 days or authority to do business is suspended.

rules.code: IF [formation state == DE] THEN [franchise tax + annual report notice]
rules.rationale: Delaware charges annual franchise tax regardless of revenue; a missed filing voids good standing.

rules.code: IF [formation state == TX] AND [entity == LLC] THEN [charging order protection]
rules.rationale: The Texas LLC statute offers strong charging-order protection worth invoking expressly.

rules.code: IF [formation state == FL] THEN [annual report deadline notice]
rules.rationale: Florida's annual report window closes May 1 and the late fee is substantial and non-waivable.

rules.code: IF [formation state == CA] OR [operating state == CA] THEN [Statement of Information notice]
rules.rationale: California requires an initial Statement of Information within 90 days of registration.

rules.code: IF [funding == VC] AND [entity == LLC] THEN [flag entity structure conflict]
rules.rationale: Institutional funds generally cannot hold LLC interests because pass-through income creates UBTI for their tax-exempt LPs.

rules.code: IF [industry == healthcare] THEN [require BAA references]
rules.rationale: HIPAA requires a Business Associate Agreement with any vendor that touches protected health information.

rules.code: IF [industry == construction] THEN [add lien and retainage provisions]
rules.rationale: Mechanics lien rights are deadline-driven and waived by silence in most states.

rules.code: IF [industry == professional services] THEN [add licensure and scope provisions]
rules.rationale: Licensed practice areas restrict non-licensee ownership in several states.

rules.code: IF [industry in {SaaS, e-commerce, healthcare}] THEN [add privacy program obligations]
rules.rationale: These businesses process personal data at volume and fall under state privacy statutes at low thresholds.

rules.code: IF [package == formation] THEN [generate the formation package]
rules.rationale: Formation documents only apply when the user is standing up a new entity.

rules.code: IF [package == commercial] THEN [generate the commercial contract set]
rules.rationale: NDA, MSA, SOW, and DPA travel together — the spec's §4.3 prediction after a sales proposal.

rules.code: IF [package == hiring] THEN [generate the hiring package]
rules.rationale: Employment agreement, handbook, and equity documents are the §4.3 sequence after a first hire.

rules.code: IF [role == provider] THEN [draft provider-favorable defaults]
rules.rationale: The side drafting the agreement sets the defaults. Caps, warranties, and indemnities all flip with the role.

rules.code: IF [role == customer] THEN [draft customer-favorable defaults]
rules.rationale: Buying services calls for the mirror image: broader warranties, service levels, and audit rights.

rules.code: IF [deal size == enterprise] THEN [add audit, insurance, and elevated caps]
rules.rationale: Above roughly $500k a year, procurement expects security review, insurance certificates, and an audit right.

rules.code: IF [deal size is mid or enterprise] THEN [add a supercap for data and confidentiality breach]
rules.rationale: A single general cap is unacceptable to most buyers once data is in scope; a carve-out at a higher multiple is the standard compromise.

rules.code: IF [commercial] AND [industry processes personal data] THEN [attach a DPA]
rules.rationale: A data processing addendum is a precondition to signature for most buyers once personal data is in scope.

rules.code: IF [auto-renew selected] THEN [add renewal and non-renewal notice mechanics]
rules.rationale: Auto-renewal is enforceable only with clear notice mechanics, and several states regulate it directly.

rules.code: IF [compensation == hourly] THEN [add non-exempt wage and hour terms]
rules.rationale: Hourly workers are almost always non-exempt, which pulls in overtime, timekeeping, and break obligations.

rules.code: IF [compensation == salary] THEN [add exempt classification terms]
rules.rationale: Salary alone does not create exempt status; the duties test still has to be met and documented.

rules.code: IF [equity offered] THEN [add equity award terms]
rules.rationale: An offer that mentions equity without naming the plan, vesting, and approval path creates a promise the company may not be able to keep.

rules.code: IF [remote] THEN [add multi-state and expense reimbursement terms]
rules.rationale: A remote hire creates tax nexus, registration duties, and expense reimbursement obligations in the state where they sit.

rules.code: IF [hiring] AND [engagement == contractor] THEN [generate a contractor agreement instead]
rules.rationale: Contractor and employee documents are not interchangeable, and using the wrong one is itself evidence of misclassification.

rules.code: IF [hiring] AND [engagement == employee] THEN [generate an employment agreement]
rules.rationale: Employment agreements carry at-will language, benefits eligibility, and policy incorporation that contractor agreements must not.
